extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, publishers, and research-integrity professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative criteria for identifying and managing fake or suspicious peer reviews in journal publishing, including algorithmic detection, reviewer verification, and editorial procedures for handling alerts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowing author-recommended reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowing authors to suggest reviewers increases the chances of peer review fraud.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article states evidence is clear that author-suggested reviewers raise risk; many journals still allow suggestions (about half of ScholarOne journals). Recommendation implied: consider disallowing or tightening controls on author-suggested reviewers because it materially increases fraud risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of reviewer email / institutional address
rubrics_metrics.description: The presence of a non-institutional email address or absence of a verified institutional address can signify risk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-institutional emails are a useful indicator but are 'not fool proof' — they should be used as one factor among several rather than as a sole basis for action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Published reviewer profile / Publons verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Absence of a Publons reviewer profile with verified review history can signal a higher risk profile for a suggested reviewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reviewer profiles (Publons) to assess competency, history and availability; recognition through Publons also helps motivate reviewers to produce thoughtful reviews. However, absence of a profile alone is not decisive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-factor algorithmic evaluation (30+ factors)
rubrics_metrics.description: The fraud prevention tool evaluates 30+ factors based on web traffic, profile information, submission stats and other server data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of data sources include web traffic, profile metadata, submission statistics and server logs. The algorithm combines these indicators to identify fake profiles, impersonators and unusual activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combination of indicators to escalate risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual factors may not trigger an alert, but combined actions can increase the risk level of a submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat alerts as risk signals (like bank fraud alerts): multiple weak signals combined justify further investigation. Avoid acting on single weak indicators in isolation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous monitoring at multiple stages
rubrics_metrics.description: The detection process runs multiple times throughout the submission and review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor submissions and review activity continuously (not only at one checkpoint) so issues can be highlighted during submission rather than after publication to reduce retractions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human-in-the-loop editorial decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: The tool flags potential fraud but leaves the final decision to the journal editor and/or publisher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use algorithmic alerts to prompt editorial investigation; do not automate final outcomes without human review. Editors should interpret alerts in context before rejecting or re-reviewing manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Configurable sensitivity and user interface based on publisher feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Tool sensitivity and user interface settings should be refined with input from publishers to balance alerts and usability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tune sensitivity to manage trade-offs between false positives and false negatives. Provide publishers/journals options to adjust sensitivity and workflow integration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role-based access and configurability
rubrics_metrics.description: The tool can be configured to set report access levels by role for each individual journal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign appropriate access controls so alerts and reports are available to the right editorial/publisher roles while protecting confidentiality and workflow integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of reviewer-finding tools to reduce reliance on author suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: Publons Reviewer Locator/Connect (Reviewer Locator/Connect) helps identify the right reviewers, assess competency, history and availability, contact them and invite them to review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ precise reviewer-search tools to locate qualified reviewers and reduce dependence on potentially biased author-suggested reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detect duplicate reviewer profiles and inconsistent emails
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer databases may contain multiple entries for the same person whenever their email changes, inviting confusion and potential abuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement checks for duplicate profiles, allow reviewers to associate multiple emails (institutional and personal), and normalize identities to avoid mistaken acceptance of malicious or duplicate accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Require persistent identifiers (e.g., ORCID) for reviewers (optional mitigation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requiring ORCIDs for reviewers was suggested as a simpler approach to verify reviewer identities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORCID requirement can help spot empty or fake profiles; caution that ORCIDs can be faked or left empty, so use as one verification element rather than sole proof of identity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flagging unusual submission/review activity to prompt remedial actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Alerts about unusual activity have led to concrete editorial actions such as rejecting an already accepted but unpublished paper or ordering re-review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use alerts to trigger follow-up actions (investigation, re-review, rejection) before publication to prevent retractions and reputational harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition and incentives for reviewers to improve review quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition through services like Publons helps motivate reviewers to do a thoughtful and efficient job; some commenters proposed paying reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incentives (recognition, reputation metrics) can increase reviewer engagement and quality. Payment is raised as a possible contractual approach, but comes with different trade-offs and legal/operational implications.
